text: I took mushrooms at a friend's place with four other people. We'd planned it well, with music and snacks and a sober friend. For me, around the peak, the room filled with a feeling of judgement. Everyone looked at me as if they knew some terrible secret about me. I became sure that I had done something unforgivable, though I couldn't remember what, and that they had all gathered to confront me. Every word they said had a double meaning. When someone offered me orange juice, I thought it was poisoned as punishment. I went into the bathroom and locked the door and sat in the bathtub. The sober friend talked to me through the door for two hours, telling me they loved me. I didn't believe a single word.

Ich habe in einer Phase großer Lebenskrise allein LSD genommen, weil ich gehofft hatte, Antworten zu finden. Stattdessen bin ich in eine Gedankenschleife geraten, in der ich immer wieder dieselben Fragen gestellt habe: Wer bin ich? Was ist echt? Warum lebe ich? Jede Antwort hat sofort zu einer neuen Frage geführt, und irgendwann hat sich alles aufgelöst, auch das Ich, das die Fragen stellt. Ich lag auf dem Boden und hatte das Gefühl, dass es mich nicht gibt und nie gegeben hat. Das hat sich angefühlt wie Sterben, nur ohne Ende. Ich habe stundenlang auf die Decke gestarrt, unfähig, mich zu bewegen. Erst als es dunkel wurde und ich Hunger bekam, kam ich langsam wieder zu mir. Ich habe mir ein Brot geschmiert und dabei geweint, weil es so etwas Normales war.

This happened when I was 26, and I'm 31 now. I'll try to describe it as fully as I can, because I've only ever told pieces of it.

I was living in a shared house with four other people. One of my housemates, I'll call her R, was into psychedelics and spirituality, and she was organising a 'full moon ceremony' in the garden with some friends from her meditation group. She invited me. There would be mushroom tea and a fire. I'd only done mushrooms once before, a small amount at a festival, and I liked it. I said yes.

There were about eight of us around the fire. R made the tea in a big pot and served it in mugs. I didn't know how much was in each mug. In hindsight, I think the tea was very strong and the dosing very uneven. The first hour was lovely. We sang some songs R had taught us. The fire crackled. The moon came up over the neighbours' roofs, enormous and orange.

Then, gradually, I noticed that I couldn't follow the songs anymore. The words lost their meaning. The faces around the fire started to look like masks, flickering in the firelight, and behind each mask I sensed something else, something not human. The fire became a mouth. The moon became an eye. I felt a huge, cold attention focus on me, the same way you might focus on an insect.

I tried to say something to R, but my voice sounded wrong, deep and slow, like a recording played at the wrong speed. She smiled at me and said 'let it come'. I don't think she realised how bad it was. I started to lose the sense of where my body ended. My hands were part of the grass. My breathing was the wind. I felt myself spreading out over the garden, thinner and thinner, until there was hardly anything left. And then there was a moment, I can't say how long, when there was nothing at all. No me, no garden, no moon. Just a black, silent, infinite absence.

When I came back from that, I was in total panic. I didn't know who I was or what I was. I knew there had been a 'before', but I couldn't remember it. I had a body but didn't know how to use it. I tried to stand and fell into the flower bed. Someone helped me up and I screamed at them, because their face was a mask with nothing behind it.

I ran into the house. Inside, under the electric light, everything was even worse. The kitchen looked like a hospital, sterile and threatening. The fridge was humming a threatening note. I went to my room and locked the door. I sat on my bed and tried to remember my name. I found my wallet and looked at my ID card. The name meant nothing. The face in the photo meant nothing. I remember looking at it and thinking: this is a stranger, and I've stolen his life.

I don't know how long I sat there. At some point R knocked and asked if I was okay. I didn't answer. She went away. Later, another housemate who hadn't taken anything, I'll call him T, knocked and said he was worried, and asked if he could come in. I opened the door because his voice sounded normal. He sat with me on the floor. He didn't try to explain anything. He just talked about ordinary things: the football results, a film he'd seen, what he was going to cook tomorrow. I didn't understand most of it, but the ordinariness was like a rope. He stayed with me until it was light.

When the sun came up I knew my name again. But the feeling that it was someone else's name, that I was living in a stolen life, didn't go away with the drug. That feeling has been with me, on and off, ever since.

The next day R came to my room with a cup of tea and said it sounded like I'd had a 'beautiful ego death'. I asked her to leave. I moved out two months later.
LSD at a friend's wedding. Overwhelmed by all the people, I had a panic attack in the middle of the dance floor and thought I was dying. Spent the rest of the night in the car park.

Ich war mit meinem Partner in einem Ferienhaus und wir haben Pilze genommen. Er hat plötzlich angefangen, sehr düstere Dinge zu sagen, dass er nicht mehr leben will und dass alles sinnlos ist. Ich wusste nicht, ob das der Trip ist oder ob er das ernst meint. Ich hatte panische Angst, dass er sich etwas antut. Ich habe ihn die ganze Nacht nicht aus den Augen gelassen und alle Messer versteckt, während ich selbst mitten im Trip war und die Wände sich bewegt haben. Am nächsten Tag hat er gesagt, es sei nur der Trip gewesen, aber ich habe ihm nicht geglaubt.

I'd been working with a therapist who also offered 'psilocybin-assisted sessions' privately, which I now know was illegal and unethical. During the session, after I'd taken a high dose, she began to talk to me about her own problems, her divorce, her financial worries. I was deep in the experience and felt that it was my job to help her. Then she told me that she felt a special connection with me and held my face in her hands for a long time. I felt confused, frozen and invaded. I didn't know what was real. I lay there for hours, unable to tell her to stop, feeling that my mind was being entered by hers.

I took 4-HO-MET with a friend at his place. It's supposed to be a light, visual psychedelic. But after the peak I got very restless and couldn't stop moving. Then I became sure that there were insects under my skin. I could feel them crawling. I scratched my arms until they bled. My friend tried to stop me, and I thought he was putting more insects on me. That lasted about three hours. The next morning my arms looked like I'd fought a cat.

Ich war bei einem Freund und wir hatten LSD genommen. Irgendwann bekam ich das Gefühl, dass der Boden unter mir verschwindet und ich ins Leere falle. Ich habe mich an der Couch festgekrallt und konnte stundenlang nicht loslassen. Mein Freund war selbst zu weit weg, um mir zu helfen. Ich dachte, ich falle für immer.

I was on mushrooms at a friend's place when I got a text from my bank saying that my account had been emptied by fraud. I'd just been paid that day. In a normal state, I'd have called the bank. On mushrooms, I spiralled. I became convinced it was a sign that my whole life was collapsing, that I would lose my flat, my job, that I'd end up homeless. I saw myself sleeping in a doorway in winter, old and alone. I couldn't use my phone properly, the bank's app was a mess of moving symbols. I walked around the garden in circles for hours, crying and talking to myself. My friend tried to help but I couldn't hear anything. The next day I called the bank and they returned all the money within a week.

Wir waren zu fünft auf einer Berghütte und haben Pilze genommen. Einer von uns ist auf dem Weg zur Toilette, die draußen war, im Dunkeln einen Abhang hinuntergestürzt. Wir hörten ihn schreien und sind rausgerannt. Er lag etwa fünf Meter weiter unten und hat sich nicht mehr bewegt. Wir waren alle unter Wirkung, und keiner wusste, was zu tun ist. Ich bin mit der Handylampe zu ihm hinuntergeklettert. Er hat aus dem Kopf geblutet und war nicht ansprechbar. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass ich einen Toten anschaue, und gleichzeitig hat sich sein Gesicht im Licht der Lampe ständig verändert. Wir haben die Bergrettung gerufen, die über eine Stunde gebraucht hat. In dieser Stunde habe ich neben ihm gesessen und seine Hand gehalten und gebetet, während der Wald um mich herum lebendig wurde. Er hat überlebt, mit einem Schädelbruch und einer gebrochenen Schulter.

I'll try to tell this in order, because it's the only way I can make sense of it.

I'm a nurse, and three years ago I was at the end of a very bad year. My mother had died, my long relationship had ended, and work in the ICU during the last Covid wave had left me exhausted and numb. A colleague, also a nurse, told me about ayahuasca and how it had helped her process her grief. She gave me the contact of a group that met in a farmhouse a couple of hours from where I live. I signed up for a weekend with two ceremonies.

The first ceremony was hard but meaningful. I cried a lot about my mother, and at one point I felt her presence, warm and kind. I purged several times. I felt cleaner afterwards and I was glad I'd come.

The second night was different. The leader, a man in his sixties, said that the second night is when the medicine 'goes deeper', and he served a larger cup. About an hour after drinking, I started to see the ICU. Not as a memory, but as if I were there. The beeping of the monitors, the hiss of the ventilators, the smell of disinfectant. I saw the faces of patients I'd lost, one after another. There had been many. I'd never allowed myself to count them. In the vision they were lying in rows, and each one turned their head to look at me.

Then I saw my mother among them, in a hospital bed, on a ventilator. She had actually died at home, of cancer, not in an ICU. But in the vision she was there, and her eyes were open and terrified, and she was trying to say something and couldn't because of the tube. I was her nurse. I was supposed to help her. And I couldn't move. I stood there in my scrubs and watched the monitor flatline.

I started screaming. I was sure I was actually there. One of the helpers came and put his hand on my back and said something like 'you're safe, it's the medicine'. I couldn't hear it. His hand felt like a patient's hand, cold. I tore away from him and crawled across the floor to a corner.

After that, things fragmented. I lost any sense of being a person. I was the ICU. I was every alarm going off at once. I was the guilt of every death. I felt that I was being judged by all of the dead, and that the verdict was that I should join them. I remember thinking very clearly that the only way to make it stop was to die, and I started looking for a way out of the room. I think I tried to get to the door. Someone held me back. I fought them. I bit someone's arm, I found out later.

They had to hold me down, three of them. The leader came and sang over me and blew tobacco smoke in my face, which made me choke and feel like I was suffocating, like the patients who couldn't breathe. I could feel my lungs filling with fluid.

It lasted, I'm told, about four hours. When it finally began to ease, I was lying on a mattress in the corner, soaked in sweat and vomit, shaking. Someone had put a blanket over me. I didn't know who I was or where I was for a long time. The first thing I recognised was the smell of the woodstove, and I held on to it like a rope.

In the morning the leader told me that I had 'released a lot of collective trauma' and that I was a 'healer', and that this was my initiation. The person I had bitten had a bruise on his arm and was very kind about it. I couldn't look at anyone. I drove home, which I shouldn't have done, and I don't remember most of the drive.

Ich habe mit einem Freund 2C-B genommen. Nach einer Stunde hatte ich das Gefühl, dass mein Gesicht nicht mehr mein Gesicht ist. Ich habe im Spiegel jemanden gesehen, den ich nicht kannte, und hatte panische Angst, dass ich so bleibe. Mein Freund hat mich beruhigt, und nach ein paar Stunden war es vorbei.
